title: minmax(), auto-fit, auto-fill
learningObjectives: Explain minmax(), auto-fit, auto-fill and use CSS Grid to create responsive two-dimensional layouts.

understand.concept: minmax(min,max) defines a grid track's minimum and maximum sizing functions. repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) and auto-fill create responsive repeated tracks based on available space. auto-fit can collapse empty tracks; auto-fill preserves them in the track layout.
understand.whyItMatters: These patterns create responsive card grids without writing a breakpoint for every width. A sensible minimum prevents cards becoming too narrow, while max limits can control growth.
understand.analogy: minmax() gives each lane a lower and upper boundary; auto-fit and auto-fill decide how many repeated lanes can fit.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS Grid follows formal track sizing, placement, and alignment algorithms.

explain.narrative: The number of columns changes with available width while each card respects a 12rem minimum track size.

examples.explanation: The number of columns changes with available width while each card respects a 12rem minimum track size.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered CSS Grid example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Change auto-fit to auto-fill and compare with only two cards in a wide container. Explain the empty-track difference.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive card or dashboard layout using this concept. Test long labels and narrow viewports.
hints: Inspect grid tracks with browser developer tools.
Check implicit tracks and minimum sizing.
Keep DOM and keyboard reading order logical.

questions.prompt: Which function sets a lower and upper track-size bound?
questions.explanation: minmax() defines the minimum and maximum sizing functions for a track.

questions.prompt: What should a responsive Grid layout preserve?
options: Readable content and logical DOM order
A fixed number of columns at every width
Visual placement regardless of keyboard order
questions.answer: Readable content and logical DOM order
questions.explanation: Responsive layout should adapt while preserving access and meaningful reading order.
